rv.q: Ms. Ferran’s achievement is immeasurable, the delicate beauty of her work marking a high point of the theater season.
Ferran, whose theatrical octave range is nothing short of astonishing, earns the sentiment in a way that I wasn’t sure was possible at this stage of the play’s existence.

A testament to Williams' insight into the crushing transition between the past and the present, especially amid rapidly changing gender roles for women, the play is sharp, bold and still as devastating as ever.

An emotionally charged, relevant revival, Streetcar is a masterpiece you can’t afford to miss.
Under the brutally effective, no-frills direction of Rebecca Frecknall, this modern classic emerges as the timeless tragedy of progress it was always meant to be.
Between the acting and the staging, the Williams classic comes to life with fresh beauty and fury.
Danger comes knocking anew in Rebecca Frecknall’s searing revival of Tennessee Williams’s tragic play, starring Paul Mescal and Patsy Ferran.
Audiences watching this latest revival will receive plenty of both.
Mescal is ideally cast as the casually cruel, boorish Stanley.
So, if there’s still a ticket to be had to this “Streetcar,” go buy it!
As Blanche DuBois and Stella Kowalski, Patsy Ferran and Anjana Vasan feelingly define this fatally frayed sisterhood as the dual heartbeat of A Streetcar Named Desire.
Ms. Frecknall does not hold back.
It’s a shame that so many contemporary directors don’t seem to trust the works they stage, laboring so furiously to improve them that they wind up merely diminishing them in the process.

The British director Rebecca Frecknall has unearthed new depths in Tennessee Williams’s A Streetcar Named Desire, turning a classic that can be played as maudlin melodrama into a kinetic prize fight between two mismatched sparring partners.

Streetcar has the additional depth and richness of Williams at his best; one of the standout aspects of this production—thanks again to the actors' and Frecknall's care—is the breadth of Williams' language.
This Streetcar is a gripping realization that makes new a play many of us feel we know inside out.

vr.q: this is hands down the best production of Streetcar named Desire I've ever seen
If you can, definitely see this production.
